objective: Preregister 20 candidates -- 8 primary option-expiration-week calendar candidates (OPEX_{SPY,QQQ,DIA,IWM}_{WEEK,WEEKMON}, long-only during the week containing the month's 3rd Friday, cash otherwise) plus 12 internal placebo controls (PLACEBO_W{1,2,4}_{SPY,QQQ,DIA,IWM} anchored to non-expiration Friday weeks) -- to resolve reports/research/harvest/coverage.json's flows_structural.rebalance_and_hedging_flows gap and reports/research/harvest/directions.jsonl's dir:option_expiration_week_calendar_effect (queued) via the owner's 2026-09-28 K1/K2 keep rule, without computing any Sharpe, return or backtest number in this dossier.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same frozen windows as every batch-screening round in this repo: stress 2016-05-02..2023-09-15 and anchor 2024-01-08..2026-09-17, judged on date-neutral Sharpe. D frequency with signal_dates_fn: exactly one version, no rebalance-day offset sweep (per screen_lane.py's docstring). The 2026-01-02..2026-09-17 holdout is reference-only and contaminated. Validity is limited to the local SIP daily archive's own coverage for SPY/QQQ/DIA/IWM/SHY, all long-lived and already used by S1-S3 -- no new data fetch is needed.
existing_solution_comparison: grep -ril "opex|option.expiration|third friday" reports/research/iterations reports/research/ledger found only incidental keyword hits in unrelated source snapshots (Graziani EOM-reversal, First Trust product page, a rebalance-timing-luck blog post) -- no prior local implementation or backtest of the option-expiration-week rule. `oc research directions check option expiration week` returned exactly one hit: the registry's own queued dir:option_expiration_week_calendar_effect entry added by the 2026-09-28-22 gap-search round -- a likely_repeat match against itself, not a prior distinct test. This round is therefore the first local test of this direction; no engine code is reused from a prior rotation/momentum candidate (the rule is a pure calendar-anchored long/cash switch, closest in construction to h20260928_05_batch2.py's TOM_SPY and FOMC_DRIFT_SPY calendar-anchored D-frequency candidates, whose pattern this module's signal_dates_fn/weights_fn split follows).
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether any of the 8 primary lookback-free calendar candidates actually clears K1, K2, strong_keep or watch_recent against S3's frozen reference numbers when run through the batch-screening lane under this project's 10bp/20bp next-open-fill cost contract, and whether any apparent edge survives the internal non-expiration-week placebo falsification test -- this is exactly what has not been tested locally and is what this round's screening pass computes, with no further parameter choice available to it once the manifest is frozen.
negative_experiments_checked: reports/research/control/step10-w1-cross-asset-trend-2026-09.md and multiple batch-screening rounds (e.g. h20260928_04_s3_alt_div_batch1: 19/19 refuted, closest K1 anchor Sharpe 0.96; h20260928_40_equity_etf_menus: 0/24 K1/K2, 5 watch_recent) show that many published calendar/tactical rules fail K1 under this project's frozen windows and cost contract even when the underlying academic finding is real -- a documented pattern, not assumed away here. The queue task's own precedent citation (batch2's TOM_SPY month-of-effect anchor Sharpe -0.69, FOMC_DRIFT_SPY -0.84) is the closest prior analog (another calendar-anchored D-frequency long/cash switch on SPY under the identical contract) and sets the expectation that this candidate family is also likely to fail K1/K2 -- this round exists to check, not to assume, that outcome, and the result is not to be second-guessed or the rule loosened if it repeats the pattern.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: 10bp per side primary, 20bp per side stress, signal at the session close, fill at the next session's open -- identical to the frozen S1/S2/S3 convention and every prior batch-screening round (cost-contract.json). This differs from Quantpedia's own Friday-close-to-Friday-close holding period (entry is one session later, at the next trading day's open after the pre-week signal day); this is a fixed contract constraint applied identically to every candidate in this batch and every prior screen_lane round, not a change made to help any candidate pass.
stop_condition: If none of the 8 primary candidates clears K1, K2, or reaches watch_recent (or every apparent pass is demoted by the placebo falsification rule), dir:option_expiration_week_calendar_effect is refuted for this scope and the flows_structural.rebalance_and_hedging_flows gap-search entry is closed for this specific mechanism; the next round should not re-tune this same calendar rule on this same universe without a new, distinct signal (e.g. an options-flow or dealer-gamma-positioning feature this repo's data does not yet support).

sources.claim: Long-only: go long S&P 100 stocks during the option-expiration week (the week containing the month's 3rd Friday), cash otherwise. Quantpedia summary of Stivers & Sun (2013, J. Banking & Finance) backtest 1988-2010: annualized return 9.3%, Sharpe 0.61, volatility ~8.7%, max drawdown -15.14%. Mechanism: option market-maker delta-hedge rebalancing reduces short-stock hedge positions during the expiration week.
sources.applicability: Grounds the OPEX_*_WEEK primary candidates' mechanism and calendar construction; the menu (SPY/QQQ/DIA/IWM index ETFs, not individual S&P 100 stocks) and the WEEK/WEEKMON/placebo grid are this batch's own preregistered choice.
sources.limitations: Practitioner summary, not the original paper; sample ends 2010, no recent-window figure.
sources.independent_replication: Original academic paper (Stivers & Sun 2013, J. Banking & Finance) independently located via WebSearch and cross-checked against the ScienceDirect abstract.

sources.claim: Garcia-Ares & Muravyev (2025, FMA working paper, 'Option returns: a tale of the expiration rollover day'): option-return-anomaly predictability concentrates on the 3rd-Friday expiration and ESPECIALLY the following Monday, driven by covered-call-writer rollover order imbalance overwhelming market-maker inventory capacity. Sample May 2005-Dec 2021; patterns 'remain largely robust over the entire sample period.' Studies delta-hedged OPTION returns, not raw stock/ETF returns; no long-only stock Sharpe/CAGR is reported by this paper.
sources.applicability: Grounds the OPEX_*_WEEKMON candidates' deferred exit (first trading day of the week after expiration week).
sources.limitations: Studies delta-hedged option returns, not stock/ETF direction; WebFetch could not parse the raw PDF, full text was extracted via curl+pdftotext instead.
sources.independent_replication: n/a -- used for mechanism support (recent sample) only; this batch's own backtest is the decisive test on stock/ETF returns.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Run all 20 candidates through the batch-screening lane (scripts/screen_batch.py --batch h20260928_42_opex_week --iteration h20260928_42_opex_week) against S3's frozen stress/anchor windows and check K1/K2/placebo-falsification directly; the engine and cost/fill convention are already frozen and reused unedited, so this is the cheapest possible resolution.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one of the 8 primary candidates clears K1 or K2 in candidate-manifest.json's keep_rule AND is not demoted by the placebo internal falsification rule.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: None of the 8 primary candidates has a date-neutral Sharpe >=80% of S3's in both windows with positive 20bp CAGR (K1), none of their 63-session inverse-vol blends with S3 beats a vol-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control by >=0.05 Sharpe in both windows (K2), none reaches watch_recent (anchor-only >=1.19), or every apparent pass is beaten by its own same-ticker placebo's anchor Sharpe.
